findings.summary: The fp32 upcast runs before the move to meta, so every rank builds a full fp32 copy of trainable params while rank 0 also keeps the old low-precision original_sd, causing a large CPU RAM spike that defeats cpu_ram_efficient_loading.

judge.reason: Claims a RAM spike from upcast ordering; not the dtype mismatch between original_sd and sharded params, and can't verify.

findings.label: unsure

findings.summary: fsdp2_load_full_state_dict casts full_sd to the model's current dtype (fp32 after upcast), so loaded values keep only bf16 precision and fp32 master weights gain nothing from the checkpoint.

judge.reason: Precision-loss claim is speculative; checkpoint values are already bf16, and it isn't the stale original_sd dtype mismatch.

findings.label: false_alarm

findings.summary: Only requires_grad params are upcast, so frozen params (e.g. LoRA base weights) stay bf16 while trainable ones become fp32, leaving mixed dtypes in an FSDP2 group that may need uniform dtype; tests don't cover this case.

judge.reason: Mixed dtype concern is speculative and differs from the original_sd stale dtype/broadcast hang bug.

findings.label: unsure
